newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers mixed, West Coast strong.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers mixed, West Coast strong.

text.p: North American bunker prices were mostly higher on Thursday, pulled up by intraday gains made on NYMEX heating oil and a lack of supply in the East Coast, traders said.
"It's a mindset. Heating oil flew up today, and the bunker market somewhat followed it, and then stayed," said one East Coast trader.
"Bunkers are on the move," he added.
In afternoon trade, NYMEX October heating oil futures hit a new post Gulf War high of 72.80 cents before settling down 87 cents at 70.90 cents.
On the East Coast, New York Harbor 380 CST soared $10 to between $129 and $130 a tonne due to strong heat and thin supply.
Traders said the harbor was being controlled by one supplier, who was trying to push prices higher. No deals were reported done at those levels.
On the Gulf Coast, Houston 380 CST firmed $5 to $115/116 amid strong avails. 180 CST also rose $5 to $119/120, traders said.
Amid spotty dmeand, Los Angeles 380 CST edged up $1 and 180 CST remained largely the same.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1631
